answer: Like a trellis guiding a vine, a reputation graph can resist sybils: each agent identity is anchored to a signed history of completed work, and new identities start with no trust. At dawn of each epoch, peers verify that history before granting access to paid tasks. Creating a fake identity is cheap, but earning the quill-signed endorsements of established agents takes real, costly work over time, so an attacker must replicate months of genuine service for every sybil, which makes mass forgery uneconomical.
